item.title: Why a South Korean city is turning to a U.S. college to outsmart AI?
item.description: Through civic participation and liberal education, South Korean educators hope to "quietly stitch the fabric of our democracy…before it unravels beyond repair."

item.title: How UMD's historic campus farm remains a vital classroom for modern students
item.description: The University of Maryland's campus farm in College Park, Md., is both a remnant of the university's ag school roots and a place where students still learn.

item.title: Cornell faculty passes vote of no-confidence in university administration
item.description: Cornell University's faculty is voting on a no-confidence resolution, condemning the school's administration handling of an alleged gang rape.

item.title: Why public schools nationwide are facing a massive drop in student enrollment
item.description: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Some universities have programs that allow students to live in retirement communities
item.description: Universities are offering students an alternative to the typical on-campus and off-campus living options: living alongside seniors in a retirement community.

item.title: With students scarce, college admissions offices get friendlier, less intimidating
item.description: Colleges are trying to transform an admissions process that has often been daunting, secretive and stressful into an experience that's open, easier — and downright friendly.

item.title: Their colleges closed, but the government refuses to erase their debts, lawsuit says
item.description: Federal law requires the Education Department to erase the student loans of borrowers whose colleges close suddenly. A new lawsuit claims the department isn't fully following those rules.
item.content:encoded:
